transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Well… I’m here because this has gotten kind of ridiculous, honestly. I’ve reached the point where I plan almost my whole summer around avoiding wasps. Like, I think about where I’m going to sit, which door I’m going to use, whether I can be outside at all if I hear buzzing.

I used to help with the garden jobs at church, and I’ve pretty much given that up because I just can’t make myself do it when wasps might be around. And even at home, if there’s buzzing near the back porch, I make my husband unload things instead of me going out there. I know that probably sounds excessive, but in the moment I just feel like I have to avoid it.
When you see a wasp or even think there might be one nearby, do you feel an immediate surge of anxiety or fear?

Yes, definitely. It’s almost instant. Like if I’m out by the porch and I hear that sharp little buzzing sound, before I even really see anything, my heart just jumps. And if I do see one hovering around the flowers or near the steps, my hands start shaking and I get this feeling like, “I need to get inside right now.” It’s not like I calmly decide to move away — it feels like my body reacts before I can think it through.
